'''''Guzmania''''' ('''tufted airplant''') is a [[genus]] of over 120 [[species]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the botanical [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Bromeliaceae, subfamily [[Tillandsioideae]].<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> They are mainly stemless, [[evergreen]], [[epiphytic]] [[perennial plant|perennial]]s [[native plant|native]] to [[Brazil]], southern [[Mexico]], [[Central America]], and northern and western [[South America]].<ref name=n>[https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=247418 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=114216 Flora of North America, ''Guzmania'' Ruiz & Pávon, Flora Peruviana. 3: 37. 1802. ]</ref> They are found at altitudes of up to {{convert|3500|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} in the Andean [[rainforest]]s.<ref name=RHSAZ />

The genus is named after Spanish-Ecuadorian [[pharmacist]] and [[naturalist]], {{interlanguage link|Anastasio Guzmán|es}}.<ref>{{cite news|url-access= |via=|access-date=|newspaper=[[Manila Bulletin]]|title=The Colors of Guzmania Bromeliads|date=18 January 2012|url=https://www.questia.com/article/1G1-292806050/the-colors-of-guzmania-bromeliads}}{{dl|date=July 2021}}</ref>

Several [[species]] of this genus are cultivated as indoor and outdoor garden plants. The best known is ''[[Guzmania lingulata]]'' (scarlet star) which bears orange and red bracts.

The plant dies after it has produced its flowers in summer, but new plants can easily be propagated from the [[Offset (botany)|offsets]] which appear as the parent plant dies. They are [[epiphytes]] and can do well if tied on to pieces of bark with roots bound into sphagnum moss.

Guzmanias require warm temperatures and relatively high humidity. The [[ascomycete]] fungus ''[[Cochliobolus sativus]]'' and other pathogens can cause fatal [[root rot]] in plants of this genus if the roots get too wet and cold.{{cite-needed|date=January 2024}}
